llm_response.content:
Empirical Research Plan ­– “The Local Labour-Market Effects of the China Trade Shock”

=========================================================
1. Identification Strategy
---------------------------------------------------------
Chosen method: Two–way-fixed-effects difference-in-differences (DID) with an instrumental-variables (IV) first stage — i.e. a shift-share (Bartik-type) instrument estimated in 2SLS.

Rationale  
• Outcome data are observed for two long-differences (1990-2000, 2000-2007) across 722 commuting zones (CZs) ⇒ panel with N≫T.  
• The policy/event (China’s export surge) was common to the whole U.S.; what differed ex-ante was each CZ’s industrial composition. This is the classic setting for a “regional exposure” DID.  
• U.S. import growth from China is potentially endogenous to U.S. demand conditions (reverse causality) and measurement error. An IV that uses Chinese export growth to *other* high-income markets removes this link.  
• Thus: (i) first-stage predicts CZ-specific import exposure using the shift-share IV; (ii) second-stage regresses changes in labour-market outcomes on predicted exposure, with CZ and period fixed effects.

=========================================================
2. Treatment and Control
---------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable (continuous “dose”)
ΔIPW_cτ = Σ_j θ_cj,1990 × ΔM̂_jτ / L_c,1990  
where  
– θ_cj,1990 = share of CZ c’s employment in industry j in 1990,  
– ΔM̂_jτ = growth of Chinese exports in industry j *to the U.S.* over period τ,  
– L_c,1990 = 1990 CZ employment.  
Units: dollars (or $1,000s) of imports per worker.

Instrument (shift-share)  
Z_cτ = Σ_j θ_cj,1990 × ΔM*_jτ  
where ΔM*_jτ is Chinese export growth to the *eight other high-income countries* listed.  

Control group / counterfactual  
CZs with little or no predicted exposure (bottom quartile of Z_cτ) provide the implicit counterfactual. With a continuous treatment, identification comes from cross-CZ heterogeneity in predicted exposure, not a discrete “treated vs. untreated” split.

Timing  
Two stacked ten-to-seven-year differences: 1990–2000 (τ=1) and 2000–2007 (τ=2). Pre-period 1980–1990 will be used for placebo tests.

=========================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
---------------------------------------------------------
A1. Exogeneity (IV exclusion)  
Growth of Chinese exports to *other* high-income markets is unrelated to latent shocks affecting U.S. CZ labour-market outcomes, conditional on CZ and period fixed effects.

Plausibility: high. Foreign demand conditions differ from U.S.-specific shocks; internal Chinese reforms and WTO entry were supply-driven.

A2. Relevance  
Industrial variation in Chinese exports to other markets must predict U.S. import growth (first-stage F > 10). Likely satisfied given 1,156 % surge.

A3. Parallel-trends / common shocks (DID)  
In absence of differential import exposure, CZs would follow parallel outcome trends. Partially testable via comparing 1980–1990 placebo period.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA)  
No spillovers across CZs (e.g., migrant labour or firm relocation that transmits shocks). Plausibility moderate; will address by controlling for contemporaneous internal migration flows.

A5. No endogenous industry re-weighting  
Baseline 1990 industry shares θ_cj are pre-determined with respect to post-1990 trade shock.

=========================================================
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
---------------------------------------------------------
T1. Pre-existing differential trends  
• Test: placebo regression 1980–1990.  
• Remedy: add lagged CZ covariates (1980–1990 Δ outcomes) and region×period trends.

T2. Selective internal migration dilutes local effects  
• Analyse migration flows; include net in-/out-migration as outcome and control.  
• Estimate effects on native residents only (using IPUMS person weights based on state of birth).

T3. Other contemporaneous shocks (offshoring to Mexico, automation)  
• Add controls for change in computer adoption, robot penetration, NAFTA-related Mexican import exposure (constructed analogously).  
• Check robustness after excluding industries highly exposed to Mexico.

=========================================================
5. R Code Outline
---------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)     # fast FE + IV
library(readr)

# 1. Load data (assuming wide CZ×period CSVs)
cz   <- fread("cz_covariates.csv")       # demographic & outcomes
trade_us <- fread("china_imports_us.csv")      # HS6→industry
trade_oecd <- fread("china_imports_oecd.csv")  # other 8 countries
emp90 <- fread("industry_emp_1990.csv")

# 2. Construct treatment and instrument -----------------------------

# a) merge industry employment shares
emp90[, theta := emp_j_cz / sum(emp_j_cz), by = cz]

# b) industry-level import growth to US and to other markets
trade_us[, dM_us := import_2000 - import_1990]
trade_oecd[, dM_oecd := import_2000 - import_1990]

# c) shift-share at CZ×period
treat <- merge(emp90[,.(cz, industry, theta)],
               trade_us[,.(industry, dM_us)],
               by="industry")[,.(DImp= sum(theta*dM_us)), cz]

instr <- merge(emp90[,.(cz, industry, theta)],
               trade_oecd[,.(industry, dM_oecd)],
               by="industry")[,.(Z= sum(theta*dM_oecd)), cz]

# d) standardise per worker
treat <- merge(treat, cz[,.(cz, L1990)], by="cz")
instr <- merge(instr, cz[,.(cz, L1990)], by="cz")
treat[, dIPW := DImp/L1990]
instr[, Z := Z/L1990]

cz <- merge(cz, treat[,.(cz,dIPW)], by="cz")
cz <- merge(cz, instr[,.(cz,Z)],  by="cz")

# 3. Stack long differences 1990-2000 and 2000-07
# (Assume already long-diffed data: variable_dlf)

# 4. Main 2SLS regression ------------------------------------------
reg_main <- feols(d_outcome ~ 1 | cz + period ~ dIPW | Z, data=cz, 
                  cluster = ~cz)
summary(reg_main)

# 5. Robustness: placebo 1980-1990
reg_placebo <- feols(d_outcome_80_90 ~ 1 | cz  ~ dIPW | Z, 
                     data=cz_80_90, cluster=~cz)
summary(reg_placebo)

# Optional: add controls and compare
reg_ctrl <- update(reg_main, . ~ . + d_robot_penetration + d_mexico_ipw)
```

=========================================================
6. Expected Results
---------------------------------------------------------
Economic theory (Stolper-Samuelson) predicts that import competition from a labour-abundant country lowers relative demand for U.S. low-skill labour.

Prior on magnitudes (per $1,000 increase in import exposure per worker):  
• Manufacturing employment : −0.8 pp of working-age pop.  
• Average weekly wage : −0.4 %.  
• Household income : −$130 (2007 $).  
• Transfers per capita : +$50 (UI, SSDI, SNAP).  
These are ball-park figures consistent with mid-range estimates in trade-labour literature.

=========================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (IV-DID)
---------------------------------------------------------
C1. Strong first stage (F > 10) .................................... 1  
C2. Exclusion: instrument affects outcomes only via imports ........ 0.5  
C3. Parallel pre-trends (placebo OK) ............................... 1  
C4. No interference / spillovers ................................... 0.5  
C5. Robust to alternative specifications & controls ................ 1  
Overall: 4 / 5 – credible though not bullet-proof.

=========================================================
